summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for left flank pain lasting 15 days, with a history of chronic myeloid leukemia, chronic graft-versus-host disease, and prior anticoagulant use. Imaging revealed subacute fractures in the left ribs, likely due to a previous fall, which explained the pain. A new soft tissue nodule in the right breast was incidentally found on CT and recommended for mammographic follow-up. The patient also reported bilateral leg pain with ambulation, suggestive of claudication, prompting a recommendation for outpatient ankle-brachial index testing. Pain was managed with oxycodone and gabapentin, and prednisone was tapered to 30 mg daily. The patient remained stable, with no acute abdominal process, and was discharged home with follow-up plans.
